pathway.title: OPEN TEXT CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The business is a recurring franchise whose core is holding while total revenue shrinks. Cloud services and customer support made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue and contracted revenue not yet recognised was USD 4.6 billion, with 57% due within a year, so revenue visibility is good. The four core product categories, 76.79% of revenue, were flat in constant currency in fiscal 2026 and grew 2.7% in constant currency in the latest quarter, while client support fell 8.99% and licence 7.95%, so total revenue fell 4.00% in the quarter, or 1.7% in constant currency excluding divestitures. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C1; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1

- Reported revenue growth in fiscal 2026 was a currency effect, not recovery. Revenue rose 1.51%, but currency added USD 135.96 million, so revenue fell USD 57.96 million in constant currency, and customer support revenue fell 2.00% as reported and 4.8% excluding currency. The fiscal 2027 outlook expects a further USD 30 million currency drag, so creditors should read the outlook range as a decline in reported revenue of 1.65% at its midpoint. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

- Margin is the swing factor, and the company's own outlook cuts it. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.3% in fiscal 2026 and 35.8% in the latest quarter, yet the outlook of 32% to 33% on revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million implies adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million, 11.88% below fiscal 2026, and an average margin of about 31.47% for the remaining three quarters. Savings of USD 490 million to USD 550 million a year are 70% realised, so the remaining 30%, or USD 147.00 million to USD 165.00 million, cannot cover the USD 226.16 million fall; the documents do not state why the margin is guided down. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90

- Free cash flow is solid but almost all of it is paid out. Free cash flow was USD 807.52 million, 47.79% of reported EBITDA, and dividends, repurchases and treasury purchases took USD 737.67 million, or 91.35%, leaving USD 69.85 million. Debt repayments of USD 648.85 million therefore relied on USD 311.91 million of divestiture proceeds and a USD 200.85 million fall in cash. On the outlook midpoint of USD 675.00 million, the dividend of about USD 270.52 million and term loan amortisation leave about USD 368.63 million for repurchases or debt, against USD 469.31 million spent on repurchases and treasury purchases in fiscal 2026. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

- Liquidity and the maturity schedule are the main support. Cash of USD 983.29 million and the undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit that no document quantifies, and no note matures before February 2028, when USD 600 million of the 2028 notes remains outstanding; term loan amortisation is only USD 35.85 million a year, and the term loan's own maturity date is not printed. The October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes with notes due in 2031 and 2033 and extended the revolver to October 2031, subject to conditions; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Leverage has stopped falling and refinancing will get more expensive. Total debt over reported EBITDA moved from 4.16x at the 2025 year-end to 3.41x and then 3.50x, and interest cover was 5.50x. The unsecured notes of USD 3,000.00 million carry far lower coupons than the 6.70% and 7.15% on the notes issued in October 2026, so rolling them at 6.70%, an illustration because unsecured pricing is not supplied, would add about USD 80.88 million a year, or 26.95% of last twelve months' cash interest; the term loan, 27.64% of principal after the October 2026 events, floats and costs USD 15.3 million more for every rise of 100 basis points. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Financial policy is unsettled by a new chief executive and an open strategic review, and it decides whether the margin cut reaches creditors or shareholders. The enterprise assessment reports at an investor day on 10 February 2027, the repurchase plan allows purchases of up to 10% of the public float, and the quarterly dividend is USD 0.28 per share; repurchases already fell 72.12% in the latest quarter to USD 30.01 million from USD 107.63 million, which shows management can cut them. The common shares, with dividends reinvested, were worth USD 50.69 at 30 June 2026 for each USD 100 invested five years earlier, against USD 120.12 for the software index. Basis: calculation C14; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 310; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Recurring, contracted revenue is the first strength. Cloud services and support are 80.93% of revenue and contracted revenue is USD 4.6 billion, with 57% falling within a year, so a decline in new sales does not reach cash flow quickly; this supports debt service over the next twelve months, but it does not protect the base after that. Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263

Liquidity and the maturity schedule are the second strength. Cash of USD 983.29 million and an undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit, no note matures before February 2028, and the October 2026 refinancing pushed the secured maturities to 2031 and 2033; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established, so the benefit is stated on principal only. Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Cost discipline and light capital intensity are the third strength. Combined research and development and sales and marketing spending fell 1.75% and capital expenditure is 3.80% of revenue, so USD 807.52 million of free cash flow came from a business that needs little reinvestment; the limit is that most savings are already banked. Basis: calculation C11; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 236; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90

Proven access to secured funding is the fourth strength: the company issued 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes within a day of the quarter-end and extended its revolver to October 2031, which reduces refinancing risk before 2028 even though its coupons are higher than those on the unsecured notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The earnings base is the first weakness. Fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 1.51% was currency, constant-currency revenue fell USD 57.96 million, the latest quarter fell 4.00%, and the outlook lowers the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32% to 33%; implied adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million is 11.88% below fiscal 2026, so leverage rises unless debt falls. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Payouts are the second weakness: dividends, repurchases and treasury purchases took 91.35% of free cash flow, leaving USD 69.85 million, so debt reduction came from divestitures and cash; at the outlook midpoint of free cash flow, about USD 368.63 million remains after the dividend and amortisation, below the USD 469.31 million spent on repurchases in fiscal 2026. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

Refinancing cost and floating-rate exposure are the third weakness: rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from their current coupons to 6.70% would add about USD 80.88 million a year as an illustration, and the term loan, 27.64% of principal after the October 2026 events, costs USD 15.3 million more for every rise of 100 basis points; both slow the fall in interest cost that helped cash flow in fiscal 2026. Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86

Unsettled financial policy and information gaps are the fourth weakness: a new chief executive, a strategic review reporting on 10 February 2027, no stated leverage target, no executed credit documents and no unaudited covenant ratio for 30 September 2026 mean creditors cannot yet price how cash will be shared with shareholders. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The latest large acquisition was Micro Focus, completed on 31 January 2023 for USD 6.2 billion, financed in part with the Acquisition Term Loan, which allowed commitments of up to USD 3.585 billion, and USD 1.0 billion of secured notes due 2027. Since then the group has sold businesses and used the proceeds to repay debt: the Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2.275 billion in May 2024, eDOCS for USD 163.0 million in January 2026 and Vertica for USD 150.0 million in May 2026. In fiscal 2026 term loan prepayments reached USD 613.0 million, including USD 300.0 million from cash. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 271; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 273; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 299–300

On 1 October 2026, after the latest balance sheet, the company issued USD 500 million of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% senior secured notes due 2033. On 2 October 2026 it redeemed the USD 1.0 billion senior secured notes due 2027 in full and purchased and cancelled USD 300.0 million of its 2028 senior notes in a cash tender offer, and on 1 October 2026 it extended the USD 750.0 million revolver from 19 December 2028 to 1 October 2031, subject to conditions. The new notes rank equally with the senior credit facilities and are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries. The cash used beyond the proceeds is not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the source-readiness assessment of OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 for the credit snapshot pathway. It tests whether the seven supplied issuer documents can support the Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit work requested in this run. It draws no credit conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No earlier module output was supplied to this module. The run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The seven supplied documents are enough for a fundamentals-only credit snapshot of Open Text Corporation at 5 November 2026, but not for legal, ratings, market or peer work, so creditors should treat the post-October 2026 capital structure as management-described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The documents rebuild five consecutive discrete quarters to 30 September 2026, four of which tie to the audited year, and they print debt, covenant, liquidity and outlook disclosure to that date. They end one day before the issuer replaced its USD 1.0 billion secured notes, so the latest balance sheet shows the old debt stack and the new one appears only in notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Each fiscal 2026 quarter ties to its parent period. The first three quarters add to the nine-month revenue printed in the March 2026 quarterly report, the audited year less those nine months equals the fourth-quarter revenue in the latest release, and the four quarterly adjusted EBITDA figures add to the printed full-year figure. Five discrete quarters, from the quarter ended 30 September 2025 (supplied as a comparative) to the quarter ended 30 September 2026, are therefore available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Every debt instrument is listed with principal and rate at 30 June 2026 and 30 September 2026: five note series, each with its maturity date, and the Acquisition Term Loan. The term loan states a seven-year term from funding but no maturity date. Principal ties to balance-sheet carrying value at both dates, and the USD 750 million revolver had no borrowings at either date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 268–270; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest balance sheet precedes the October 2026 refinancing. On 1 October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500 million of 6.70% secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% secured notes due 2033. On 2 October 2026 it redeemed USD 1.0 billion of 2027 secured notes and purchased and cancelled USD 300 million of 2028 unsecured notes, and the revolver maturity was extended from 19 December 2028 to 1 October 2031, subject to conditions. The terms are stated, but no pro forma balance sheet is given and the cash spent on premium, accrued interest and costs is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The financial maintenance covenant the filings describe is a maximum consolidated net leverage ratio of 4.50x under both the revolver and the term loan. The issuer printed 3.35x at 31 December 2025, 3.02x at 31 March 2026 and 2.75x at 30 June 2026. For 30 September 2026 the quarterly report states compliance only, and the November 2026 release gives a net leverage ratio of 2.55x without defining it. The covenant EBITDA is defined in an agreement that was not supplied and is worded differently from the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, so a leverage figure built from adjusted EBITDA is not the covenant ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2025-12-31_otex-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-03-31_otex-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash of USD 983.3 million at 30 September 2026 and the undrawn revolver are printed. Letters of credit appear only as a type of guarantee and inside the covenant definitions, with no amount issued under the revolver, so availability net of letters of credit is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating level, market price, spread quote, peer set or portfolio input was supplied, and the filings mention ratings only as a risk factor and in forward-looking caveats. Work that needs those inputs cannot draw on this document set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, indentures and security documents are listed by reference in the annual report exhibit index but were not supplied. The annual report and the quarterly reports summarise their terms, so those summaries are the only evidence for ranking, guarantees, call terms and covenant definitions, and the terms of the October 2026 notes are set out in the notes to the November 2026 quarterly report, not in executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - From the first quarter of fiscal 2027 the issuer reports eight product categories instead of seven, and only the quarter ended 30 September 2025 was recast, so category revenue breaks between the annual report and the latest quarter while total revenue is unaffected. Ranges for fiscal 2027 revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow are printed in the annual report and maintained unchanged in the latest quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is dispersed: the largest holder in the ownership table holds 11.17% of the common shares and no sponsor is named. The chief executive changed on 20 April 2026 after a period under an interim chief executive. Statements are consolidated for Open Text Corporation, and no issuer-level or guarantor-level financial statements are printed, so structural priority rests on the notes' descriptions rather than on entity accounts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leases, pensions, purchase obligations, guarantees and the Canadian tax reassessment dispute are disclosed in the notes. The contractual-obligations tables at both dates print lease, future-lease and purchase amounts apart from debt, so each of those claims sits outside the debt figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a pass is that every document is written by the issuer, so debt terms, covenant ratios and the net leverage ratio of 2.55x are management statements that cannot be checked against executed agreements, rating agency views or market prices. A restricted verdict would also be reasonable for any work that needs the post-refinancing capital structure, because only the notes to the latest quarterly report describe it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The verdict stays at pass with limitations because the requested work is a fundamentals snapshot, and audited statements, quarterly statements, adjusted EBITDA reconciliations and the debt notes meet its evidence demands. It would move to conditional for legal or recovery work, which needs the executed documents. It would improve if a pro forma balance sheet for 2 October 2026 appeared, and the investor day scheduled for 10 February 2027 may change the strategy and the product-category basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No executed credit agreement, indenture or security document is supplied, and the run settings declare none, so terms come from the issuer's own summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No credit rating, market quote, peer set, portfolio or user assumption is supplied; a blank in the run settings is not treated as zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest balance sheet is dated 30 September 2026 and the October 2026 refinancing is described in notes only, with no pro forma balance sheet and no amount for the cash used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit issued under the revolver are not quantified in any document.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant ratio at 30 September 2026 is not printed; only compliance and an undefined net leverage ratio are stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No issuer-level or guarantor-level financial statements are printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Product-category revenue sits on two bases because only one earlier quarter was recast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Acquisition Term Loan maturity date is not printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each test uses figures printed in the sources, in thousands of US dollars unless stated, and checks that the discrete periods tie to their parent periods and that debt principal ties to carrying value.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the financial foundation for OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. It extracts the statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and cover from the supplied filings and releases, in US dollars. It makes no credit recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Open Text cut leverage to 3.50x reported EBITDA (2.90x net) at 30 September 2026 from 4.16x (3.40x net) at the 2025 fiscal year-end, with cash interest cover of 5.50x, but progress stalled in the latest quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Last-twelve-months EBITDA fell with revenue and higher special charges, so total leverage rose from 3.41x at the 2026 fiscal year-end. The October 2026 refinancing moved the nearest secured maturity from 2027 to 2031 and 2033, but the cash it used is not stated, so net debt and leverage after it are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage on carrying-value debt over reported EBITDA fell from 4.16x at the 2025 fiscal year-end to 3.41x at the 2026 fiscal year-end, as debt fell by USD 607.55 million and reported EBITDA rose by 10.16%. It then rose to 3.50x on a last-twelve-months basis at 30 September 2026, because last-twelve-months EBITDA is USD 40.13 million below the fiscal 2026 figure while debt barely moved: first-quarter revenue fell 4.00% year on year and special charges were USD 33.29 million against USD 20.14 million. Net leverage moved from 3.40x to 2.85x to 2.90x, so the deleveraging of fiscal 2026 has paused.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 233–234; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash interest paid fell from USD 352.38 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 321.69 million in fiscal 2026 and to USD 300.11 million over the last twelve months, which lifted reported EBITDA cover from 4.35x to 5.25x and 5.50x. The fall comes from the term loan, whose interest expense dropped as prepayments cut its floating-rate balance, while interest on the fixed-rate notes did not change; cash received for interest is not netted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 306; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 269–270; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 273

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow, operating cash flow less capital expenditure, was USD 807.52 million in fiscal 2026 against USD 687.40 million in fiscal 2025, a conversion of 47.79% of reported EBITDA. Dividends, share repurchases and treasury purchases took USD 737.67 million, or 91.35% of it, so debt repayment of USD 648.85 million depended on USD 311.91 million of divestiture proceeds and a USD 200.85 million fall in cash. Capital returns compete with deleveraging for the same cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity at 30 September 2026 was USD 983.29 million of cash plus the undrawn USD 750 million revolver, before letters of credit that no document quantifies. Before 2028 the only principal falling due is term loan amortisation of USD 35.85 million a year; after 2 October 2026 the nearest note maturity is the 2028 notes, with USD 600 million left after the tender. The revolver maturity was extended to 2031, subject to conditions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 268; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The latest balance sheet precedes the October 2026 refinancing. On 1 October 2026 the issuer issued USD 500 million of 6.70% secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% secured notes due 2033, and on 2 October 2026 it redeemed USD 1.0 billion of 2027 secured notes and cancelled USD 300 million of 2028 unsecured notes. Principal ends USD 300 million lower, and the new coupons of 6.70% and 7.15% straddle the 6.90% coupon on the notes redeemed. The cash paid in premium, accrued interest and costs is not stated, so pro forma net debt and leverage are not established.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Printed covenant ratios and the figures computed here are different measures. The lenders' ratio was 3.35x at 31 December 2025, 3.02x at 31 March 2026 and 2.75x at 30 June 2026, falling with debt; the last sits between net debt over reported EBITDA at 2.85x and net debt over adjusted EBITDA at 2.53x, and its definition sits in agreements that are not supplied. The release's net leverage ratio of 2.55x at 30 September 2026 equals net debt over last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA computed here, although the release does not define it. Covenant capacity is not inferred.

The first quarter drained USD 116.56 million of cash through deferred revenue, against USD 108.80 million a year earlier, and receivables collections of USD 115.80 million offset it; a shrinking float is a claim on cash that creditors do not see in debt.

fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 233–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading this as a steady deleveraging credit is the company's own fiscal 2027 outlook: revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 32% to 33%, against 36.3% in fiscal 2026 and 35.8% in the latest quarter. A lower margin on lower revenue cuts EBITDA and lifts leverage unless debt falls faster, and the latest quarter already shows that. It would take a second quarter of rising last-twelve-months EBITDA, or debt falling faster than EBITDA, to restore the fiscal 2026 trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is the maturity profile: nothing but term loan amortisation falls due before 2028, the revolver is undrawn, and the refinancing removed the nearest secured maturity. What would change the view is evidence of cash used in the refinancing large enough to lift net debt, or a covenant ratio at 30 September 2026 close to the 4.50x maximum, neither of which is printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the business, ownership and governance fact pack for OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the business model, ownership, transactions, capital allocation and sponsor and governance behaviour from the supplied filings and releases. It makes no recovery, peer or instrument recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Open Text has no sponsor and a mostly independent board, but it returned 91.35% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow to shareholders while a new chief executive and an open strategic review leave its direction unsettled, so governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: USD 613.0 million of term loan prepayments from divestiture proceeds and cash, and an October 2026 refinancing that extended maturities, sit beside a portfolio being sold down and a share count cut by 4.97% in a year. No document shows priming, an uptier or another creditor-adverse step, but the legal capacity to distribute is not established because the executed agreements are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 219

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with public shareholders, not a sponsor, and no holder is large enough to dominate the board. The four holders above 5% own 33.13% between them, the largest 11.17%, and directors and executive officers as a group 2.42%. Eleven of thirteen directors are independent; the chief executive and the chair are not. Creditors therefore face no sponsor extraction or exit-timing risk, but there is also no controlling holder whose support could be called on in stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 219; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Shareholder distributions, not debt-funded transactions, are the main governance risk to creditors. In fiscal 2026 dividends, share repurchases and treasury stock purchases took USD 737.67 million, which is 91.35% of free cash flow of USD 807.52 million, and the share count fell 4.97%. The quarterly dividend of USD 0.28 per share continues and a renewed repurchase plan allows purchases of up to 10% of the public float. Because these payments take nearly all internally generated cash, debt reduction relies on asset sales and cash on hand, not retained free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 117; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 127; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 310; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The group is deleveraging by selling businesses, which shrinks the earnings base that supports the debt. It bought Micro Focus for USD 6.2 billion in January 2023, financed in part with new secured debt, sold its Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2,275.0 million in May 2024, and sold two more businesses in fiscal 2026 for USD 313.0 million, using all of it to prepay the term loan; a further USD 300.0 million of prepayment came from cash. Management says it regularly evaluates divestitures, so more sales are likely.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 273; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 299–300; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 126; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leadership turnover and an open strategic review lower visibility of financial policy. Both the chief executive and chief financial officer roles were interim for part of fiscal 2026, the chair served as executive chair from August 2025 to June 2026 at a cost of USD 3.1 million, a new chief executive started on 20 April 2026, and an enterprise assessment launched in the fourth quarter is due to report at an investor day on 10 February 2027. Business Optimization Plan charges were USD 96.01 million in fiscal 2026 and USD 127.92 million in fiscal 2025. Capital allocation and portfolio policy may change after that date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating model is recurring but eroding at the support line. Cloud services and customer support made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue; customer support revenue fell from USD 2,713.30 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 2,287.45 million while cloud revenue grew from USD 1,820.52 million to USD 1,958.55 million. No customer exceeded 10% of receivables and the United States was 49.89% of revenue. Cloud migration is replacing support income, so cash flow is durable but its mix is changing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 261; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 305; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 239; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring but is silent on entity-level detail. The covenant maximum and the issuer's ratios, the adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, the debt terms and the sale of each business are printed, yet there are no guarantor-level statements, no letters of credit amount and no executed agreements, so who can receive value, and what the notes allow, cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A tax dispute with the Canada Revenue Agency is a claim outside debt that carries no accrual. For fiscal 2012 to 2016 the potential liability for penalties, interest and provincial taxes is about USD 87.4 million; for fiscal 2017 to 2021 the company says an adverse outcome could cut deferred tax assets by up to about USD 470 million, with cash tax over several years, and it has provisionally paid about USD 32.0 million and USD 40.3 million so far. A loss would draw on the same cash that serves debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for lower risk is behaviour: the company prepaid USD 613.0 million of its term loan in fiscal 2026, extended its nearest maturities in October 2026, has no history in these documents of exchange offers, priming or waivers, and says its focus is cash generation, debt reduction and capital allocation. That argues for Low. Evidence for High would be debt-funded distributions or acquisitions after the strategic review, use of the universal shelf registration filed in December 2025, or a repurchase programme that outruns free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view moves to Low if the investor day sets a leverage target and ranks debt reduction ahead of repurchases, and to High if the next year shows buybacks or acquisitions financed by new debt. The legal documents, which would show how much value can leave, are the missing evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The legal capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add debt or release guarantees is not established because no executed agreement is supplied, so the Medium level rests on documented behaviour and would move if baskets prove wide or tight.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The documents show conduct only from fiscal 2023, so the absence of exchange offers, priming or waivers describes these documents, not the company's full history; an earlier episode would raise the risk level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor fund, vintage or fee data exist because the company is publicly held; the sponsor assessment is therefore limited to shareholders' conduct and cannot be scored on the nine sponsor dimensions beyond those evidenced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sums invested in the strategic funds in which the company holds up to about 19.9% limited partner interests are not stated, so related-party leakage can be described but not sized, and the governance conclusion on conflicts stays qualitative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The outcome of the strategic review is not published until the investor day, so any conclusion about future capital allocation could reverse after 10 February 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The latest large acquisition was Micro Focus, completed on 31 January 2023 for USD 6.2 billion, financed in part with the Acquisition Term Loan, which allowed commitments of up to USD 3.585 billion, and USD 1.0 billion of secured notes due 2027. Since then the group has sold businesses and used the proceeds to repay debt: the Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2.275 billion in May 2024, eDOCS for USD 163.0 million in January 2026 and Vertica for USD 150.0 million in May 2026. In fiscal 2026 term loan prepayments reached USD 613.0 million, including USD 300.0 million from cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 1 October 2026, after the latest balance sheet, the company issued USD 500 million of 6.70% senior secured notes due 2031 and USD 500 million of 7.15% senior secured notes due 2033. On 2 October 2026 it redeemed the USD 1.0 billion senior secured notes due 2027 in full and purchased and cancelled USD 300.0 million of its 2028 senior notes in a cash tender offer, and on 1 October 2026 it extended the USD 750.0 million revolver from 19 December 2028 to 1 October 2031, subject to conditions. The new notes rank equally with the senior credit facilities and are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries. The cash used beyond the proceeds is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The risk level is driven by shareholder distributions that take 91.35% of free cash flow and a portfolio being sold down, because they slow deleveraging and shrink the earnings base, which implies slower improvement in leverage than cash flow alone would give. Countervailing evidence is USD 613.0 million of term loan prepayment, an October 2026 extension of maturities and the absence of any creditor-adverse step in the documents. Further analysis requires the executed credit agreement and indentures and the outcome of the strategic review.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Open Text presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the return of 91.35% of fiscal 2026 free cash flow to shareholders alongside a portfolio sold down to repay debt, which matters because it slows deleveraging and shrinks the earnings base, and implies slower improvement in leverage than cash flow alone would give. Countervailing evidence is USD 613.0 million of term loan prepayment, an October 2026 extension of maturities and the absence of any creditor-adverse step in the documents. Further analysis requires the executed agreements and the outcome of the strategic review. Governance assessment completed with limitations: Sponsor and governance risk level Medium; key gaps are the executed agreements, the strategic review outcome, fund investments and guarantor detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is the fundamental credit assessment for OPEN TEXT CORP (otex) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. It synthesises the supplied filings, releases and earlier modules into a credit view, strengths and weaknesses, a downside scenario and monitoring triggers. It makes no rating, legal-capacity, recovery or portfolio recommendation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Open Text is an adequate credit: recurring software revenue and no note maturity before 2028 protect liquidity, but a shrinking earnings base and payouts taking 91.35% of free cash flow leave creditors relying on asset sales, not retained cash, to cut debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was 2.90x reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026 against 2.85x at the 2026 year-end, so deleveraging has paused, and pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established. The outlook lowers the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32% to 33% from 36.3% and free cash flow to USD 625 million to USD 725 million from USD 807.52 million, which is the main reason leverage rises unless debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is a recurring franchise whose core is holding while total revenue shrinks. Cloud services and customer support made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue and contracted revenue not yet recognised was USD 4.6 billion, with 57% due within a year, so revenue visibility is good. The four core product categories, 76.79% of revenue, were flat in constant currency in fiscal 2026 and grew 2.7% in constant currency in the latest quarter, while client support fell 8.99% and licence 7.95%, so total revenue fell 4.00% in the quarter, or 1.7% in constant currency excluding divestitures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C1; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reported revenue growth in fiscal 2026 was a currency effect, not recovery. Revenue rose 1.51%, but currency added USD 135.96 million, so revenue fell USD 57.96 million in constant currency, and customer support revenue fell 2.00% as reported and 4.8% excluding currency. The fiscal 2027 outlook expects a further USD 30 million currency drag, so creditors should read the outlook range as a decline in reported revenue of 1.65% at its midpoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin is the swing factor, and the company's own outlook cuts it. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 36.3% in fiscal 2026 and 35.8% in the latest quarter, yet the outlook of 32% to 33% on revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million implies adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million, 11.88% below fiscal 2026, and an average margin of about 31.47% for the remaining three quarters. Savings of USD 490 million to USD 550 million a year are 70% realised, so the remaining 30%, or USD 147.00 million to USD 165.00 million, cannot cover the USD 226.16 million fall; the documents do not state why the margin is guided down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Free cash flow is solid but almost all of it is paid out. Free cash flow was USD 807.52 million, 47.79% of reported EBITDA, and dividends, repurchases and treasury purchases took USD 737.67 million, or 91.35%, leaving USD 69.85 million. Debt repayments of USD 648.85 million therefore relied on USD 311.91 million of divestiture proceeds and a USD 200.85 million fall in cash. On the outlook midpoint of USD 675.00 million, the dividend of about USD 270.52 million and term loan amortisation leave about USD 368.63 million for repurchases or debt, against USD 469.31 million spent on repurchases and treasury purchases in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 136; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity and the maturity schedule are the main support. Cash of USD 983.29 million and the undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit that no document quantifies, and no note matures before February 2028, when USD 600 million of the 2028 notes remains outstanding; term loan amortisation is only USD 35.85 million a year, and the term loan's own maturity date is not printed. The October 2026 refinancing replaced the 2027 secured notes with notes due in 2031 and 2033 and extended the revolver to October 2031, subject to conditions; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage has stopped falling and refinancing will get more expensive. Total debt over reported EBITDA moved from 4.16x at the 2025 year-end to 3.41x and then 3.50x, and interest cover was 5.50x. The unsecured notes of USD 3,000.00 million carry far lower coupons than the 6.70% and 7.15% on the notes issued in October 2026, so rolling them at 6.70%, an illustration because unsecured pricing is not supplied, would add about USD 80.88 million a year, or 26.95% of last twelve months' cash interest; the term loan, 27.64% of principal after the October 2026 events, floats and costs USD 15.3 million more for every rise of 100 basis points.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 85–86; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy is unsettled by a new chief executive and an open strategic review, and it decides whether the margin cut reaches creditors or shareholders. The enterprise assessment reports at an investor day on 10 February 2027, the repurchase plan allows purchases of up to 10% of the public float, and the quarterly dividend is USD 0.28 per share; repurchases already fell 72.12% in the latest quarter to USD 30.01 million from USD 107.63 million, which shows management can cut them. The common shares, with dividends reinvested, were worth USD 50.69 at 30 June 2026 for each USD 100 invested five years earlier, against USD 120.12 for the software index.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 310; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is operating momentum and execution on debt. Core revenue grew 2.4% and core cloud revenue 11.2% in the latest quarter, enterprise cloud bookings rose 22.55%, free cash flow rose in the latest quarter, and the company cut debt by USD 607.55 million in fiscal 2026 and completed a refinancing within a day of the quarter-end. The guided margin step-down is also hard to reconcile with a margin of 35.8% in the quarter just reported: the outlook implies about 30.80% to 32.13% for the remaining quarters, so if the company simply repeats the latest quarter, adjusted EBITDA ends well above the outlook and leverage falls. The view would improve if the next two quarters hold a margin close to the latest quarter's 35.8%, if cloud net renewal returns to 96% from 94%, or if the investor day names a leverage target and ranks debt reduction ahead of repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if the margin lands at or below the 32% to 33% range with support revenue falling faster than cloud grows, if free cash flow comes in at the low end of USD 625 million to USD 725 million while repurchases continue, if the enterprise assessment leads to a debt-funded acquisition or a larger payout, or if the covenant ratio for 30 September 2026, which is not printed, proves well above the 2.75x printed for the 2026 year-end. None of these is shown in the documents yet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 124; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The assessment that refinancing capacity is adequate rests on one completed issue in October 2026 and on the company's own statements, because no credit rating, secondary price or spread is supplied; market levels well above the 6.70% and 7.15% coupons would lower that assessment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The finding that margin is the swing factor takes the company's outlook as given, and the documents do not explain why the margin is guided below the latest quarter, so the finding is too cautious if the guidance is conservative and not cautious enough if it reflects costs not yet disclosed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside arithmetic holds net debt at its 30 September 2026 level, so it overstates leverage if free cash flow retires debt and understates it if the October 2026 refinancing used cash; the cash used is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The assessment that the core is holding rests on the company's own renewal rates, which exclude small-business and consumer clients and migrations to cloud, and on its own competitor list; no market share, pricing or third-party data is supplied, so the finding cannot be tested against peers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Open Text supplies data management software to large and regulated organisations, so its credit case rests on how sticky that revenue is. Cloud services and customer support, which renew, made up 80.93% of fiscal 2026 revenue, enterprise clients contribute about 90% of revenue, no customer exceeded a tenth of receivables, and the United States is 49.89% of revenue with most of the rest in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. That mix supports cash-flow visibility and debt service, but growth now has to come from moving support clients to cloud, which carries a lower gross margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 104; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group has changed shape since the Micro Focus acquisition for USD 6.2 billion in January 2023: it sold the Application Modernization and Connectivity business for USD 2,275.0 million in May 2024 and two more businesses for USD 313.0 million in fiscal 2026, and used the proceeds to repay the term loan. The earnings base is smaller and rests on the four core categories, 76.79% of revenue, while the lines that are shrinking or being sold are 23.21%; further disposals are possible after the strategic review, which would shrink the base again.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control sits with public shareholders: the largest holder has 11.17%, no sponsor is named, and eleven of thirteen directors are independent, so creditors face no sponsor extraction but also no owner to call on in stress. The group is one consolidated credit whose notes are guaranteed by subsidiaries, and no guarantor-level statements are supplied, so which entity ranks where rests on the notes' own descriptions. Financial policy is the weak point: payouts took 91.35% of free cash flow, a repurchase plan of up to 10% of the public float runs to August 2027, a new chief executive started on 20 April 2026, the strategic review reports on 10 February 2027, and no leverage target appears in the documents, so leverage tolerance is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 214; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is mostly recurring and well covered for twelve months, but the base is not growing. Recurring revenue is 80.93% of the total, support agreements run for twelve months and renew at the client's option, and contracted revenue of USD 4.6 billion has 57% falling due within a year. The support net renewal rate rose to 93% from 91%, while the cloud net renewal rate fell to 94% from 96%, and both exclude small-business and consumer clients and migrations to cloud. Because net renewal is below full retention, some recurring revenue has to be replaced every year; enterprise cloud bookings of USD 946.7 million against USD 772.5 million, up 22.55%, are the main source of replacement, so durability beyond a year depends on bookings continuing to outrun support attrition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C15; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 106

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported growth overstates the trend. Fiscal 2026 revenue rose 1.51% as reported, but currency added USD 135.96 million and constant-currency revenue fell USD 57.96 million; customer support fell 4.8% excluding currency. The outlook assumes the core categories grow 2% to 3% in constant currency after being flat in fiscal 2026, and the latest quarter's 2.7% is supportive but is one quarter of evidence. Pricing power is not stated: the documents give no price increase or churn split beyond the net renewal rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C2; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin has been defended by cost cuts, not by pricing, and the room left is limited. Gross margin was 73.74%, with 90% on customer support and 64% on cloud, so each dollar that moves from support to cloud lowers gross margin by about 26 percentage points before any cost saving. Research and development and sales and marketing together fell 1.75% in fiscal 2026 as the Business Optimization Plan removed labour cost, and the adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 36.3% from 34.1% in fiscal 2024. The plan's remaining savings are USD 147.00 million to USD 165.00 million and its remaining cost is USD 23.80 million, after the expected total cost was raised to USD 270.0 million from USD 260.0 million; special charges were USD 33.29 million in the latest quarter against USD 20.14 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 106–107; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 297; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is light but rose: capital expenditure was USD 199.30 million, or 3.80% of revenue, and maintenance and growth spending are not split, so how much of it could be cut in a downturn is not established. Operating leverage works against the company when revenue falls, because personnel cost is largely fixed in the short run and the plan's workforce reductions have already been made.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 236; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is moderate and heavily taxed. Reported EBITDA of USD 1,689.75 million became free cash flow of USD 807.52 million after net cash interest of USD 279.72 million, cash taxes of USD 300.06 million and capital expenditure of USD 199.30 million, with other operating items, mainly working capital and restructuring cash, absorbing USD 103.15 million. Free cash flow was 47.79% of reported EBITDA, or 42.43% of adjusted EBITDA, and it was the only fiscal 2026 outlook metric the company missed, which it blamed on the timing of year-end receipts. Cash taxes rose 6.31% in the latest quarter, so tax absorbs cash ahead of debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C14; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 306; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The interest-free float is shrinking: deferred revenue fell from USD 1,684.14 million at the 2025 year-end to USD 1,643.15 million and then USD 1,529.69 million at 30 September 2026, and the first quarter drained USD 116.56 million of cash through that line, so each year the company must win new prepayments just to hold cash. Contractual debt payments, principal and interest, due in fiscal 2027 were USD 319.53 million at the 2026 year-end, of which interest is about USD 283.68 million, before the October 2026 refinancing. Claims outside debt are small against cash flow except one: the pension liability is USD 100.47 million, operating lease liabilities USD 202.04 million, purchase obligations USD 257.76 million, and the Canada Revenue Agency matter could cut deferred tax assets by up to USD 470 million with a later cash tax effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 233; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 285–286; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is intense and widening. The company names IBM, Microsoft, Oracle and ServiceNow among large rivals, competes with Microsoft while also partnering with it, and says AI has extended competition to platform providers and specialist knowledge platforms, so pricing and renewal terms are contested in every category. New entrants matter mainly through AI: they target the same unstructured-data workloads, which pressures the cloud net renewal rate that already slipped to 94%. Substitutes are the sharpest threat, because the company itself warns that clients may build internal AI alternatives, which would hit licence and support revenue first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is moderate: enterprise clients are about 90% of revenue and support renews annually at their option, which lets them push on price at renewal, but no customer is concentrated enough to threaten cash flow. Supplier power is limited: cloud cost of revenues comprises third-party network usage fees, data centre maintenance and support staff, and the network fees rose USD 6.5 million in fiscal 2026, so supplier pricing is a small drag on the 64% cloud margin, not a credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials, with currency as the exception. Revenue outside the United States is 50.11%, the outlook includes an unfavourable currency effect of about USD 30 million, or 0.57% of fiscal 2026 revenue, and fiscal 2026 growth was flattered by currency as shown above. Tariff and trade tensions are flagged as a risk, but the documents give no amount, and AI regulation and technology change are addressed under competitive forces.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: recurring revenue of 80.93% with USD 4.6 billion of contracted revenue gives cash-flow visibility; liquidity of USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit and no note due before 2028 protect near-term debt service; capital intensity of 3.80% of revenue keeps conversion high; and no customer concentration limits single-client risk. Each supports debt service in the next twelve to twenty-four months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C11; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses: a shrinking earnings base with an outlook that lowers margin; payouts of 91.35% of free cash flow that leave only USD 69.85 million for debt reduction; a floating-rate term loan that is 27.64% of principal; and a financial policy that is unsettled until the investor day. Each lowers the pace of deleveraging or raises its cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities: core cloud growth of 11.2%, enterprise cloud bookings up 22.55% and remaining plan savings of USD 147.00 million to USD 165.00 million could lift margin; an investor day that sets a leverage target and ranks debt reduction first would improve creditor alignment. Only these could improve credit quality.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C11; calculation C15; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 90

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats: AI substitution and platform rivals that lower renewal rates; support attrition that outruns cloud growth; refinancing of USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes at coupons well above those they now carry; and further disposals that shrink earnings. Each would weaken cash flow or raise interest cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On a ratings-style reading, scale and liquidity are strong, competitive advantage, diversification, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability and access to capital markets are average, and financial policy and governance is weak. Scale is strong because revenue of USD 5,246.40 million, about 90% from enterprise clients, spreads fixed costs and client risk widely, although it is shrinking; competitive advantage is average because embedded data management supports renewal but the cloud net renewal rate of 94% and AI rivals contest it; diversification is average because content alone is 42.70% of revenue and the United States is 49.89%, offset by no single-customer concentration.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C2; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 263

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost and capex flexibility is average because savings are mostly taken and capital intensity of 3.80% leaves little to cut; margin stability is average because the margin rose to 36.3% but is guided to 32% to 33%; free cash flow stability is average because USD 807.52 million fell short of its outlook and the next outlook is USD 625 million to USD 725 million, with taxes and interest taking a large share before it. Access to capital markets is average, not strong: the October 2026 issue shows access, but at 6.70% and 7.15% against far lower coupons on the notes it follows, and no rating or price is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C10; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is strong because cash of USD 983.29 million and the undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit, against USD 35.85 million of annual term loan amortisation and USD 600 million of 2028 notes due in February 2028; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established. Financial policy and governance is weak because payouts took 91.35% of free cash flow, and the strategic review and a new chief executive leave policy unsettled. The trend is improved in fiscal 2026, with total debt over reported EBITDA at 3.41x against 4.16x, but stalled at 3.50x in the latest quarter. The datapoints that would settle the view are pro forma net debt, the covenant ratio for 30 September 2026, the executed credit documents, the letters of credit issued and a rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next twelve to twenty-four months look manageable for debt service and uncomfortable for leverage. The outlook for fiscal 2027 is revenue of USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million, adjusted EBITDA margin of 32% to 33% and free cash flow of USD 625 million to USD 725 million; the margin and cash flow guidance are lower than fiscal 2026 while the core categories are guided to grow 2% to 3%. Tailwinds are core cloud growth of 11.2%, enterprise cloud bookings up 22.55%, plan savings still to come and a maturity schedule with USD 35.85 million of amortisation and USD 600 million of notes before 2029. Headwinds are support attrition, a currency drag of USD 30 million, rising cash taxes and the likelihood that the next refinancings cost more; with net debt held at its 30 September 2026 level, net debt over the outlook adjusted EBITDA midpoint would be 2.85x against 2.55x reported, and 2.91x at the low end, so leverage rises unless debt falls, and pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 1; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the notes due from 2029 to 2033 and the term loan fall due, and the outcome depends on whether cloud and AI products turn the core into a growing base and whether the review sets a deleveraging priority. The unsecured notes of USD 3,000.00 million will refinance in the same window at coupons the October 2026 issue suggests are higher, adding about USD 80.88 million a year at 6.70%, an illustration only; if earnings are lower by then, the cost lands on a smaller cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with support attrition outrunning cloud migration. In the latest quarter client support fell 8.99% and licence 7.95%, cloud grew only 4.33%, and total revenue fell 4.00%; if that pace continued, revenue would fall below the USD 5,135 million to USD 5,185 million outlook, whose low end is USD 5,135 million, and the cloud net renewal rate at 94% would show the migration failing to replace the loss. The first operating break is margin: cloud carries a 64% gross margin against 90% for support, the plan's remaining savings of USD 147.00 million to USD 165.00 million are smaller than the USD 226.16 million gap to fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA, and the outlook already assumes a margin of about 31.47% for the rest of the year; at the low end of the outlook adjusted EBITDA is USD 1,643.20 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C4; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 106–107; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial transmission runs through cash flow: at the low end of the USD 625 million to USD 725 million outlook, the dividend of about USD 270.52 million and term loan amortisation leave about USD 318.63 million for repurchases and debt, so either repurchases are cut or cash falls. Leverage rises mechanically, since net debt held at its 30 September 2026 level would be 2.91x the low-end adjusted EBITDA against 2.55x now; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established. Liquidity does not fail in this path: USD 1,733.29 million is available before letters of credit, no note matures before February 2028, and management has levers in repurchases, which already fell 72.12% in the latest quarter, capital expenditure, the dividend and further disposals. The observable triggers are quarterly client support and cloud revenue, the net renewal rates, free cash flow against the outlook floor, the covenant ratio when printed, and the investor day on 10 February 2027. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, but not to keep leverage falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Open Text presents an adequate business profile supported by recurring revenue of 80.93% of sales, contracted revenue of USD 4.6 billion, liquidity of USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit and no note maturity before 2028, but credit quality is constrained by a shrinking earnings base, an outlook that lowers margin and free cash flow, payouts of 91.35% of free cash flow and an unsettled financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, because free cash flow of USD 807.52 million is generated after interest, taxes and capital expenditure, but most of it is paid out. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the pace of deleveraging, the cost of rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from 2028, the price of the next issue relative to the 6.70% and 7.15% paid in October 2026, and the investor day. The primary downside path is support attrition outrunning cloud growth with margin at the low end of the outlook, lifting net leverage toward 2.91x on current net debt while payouts continue. Further analysis would require pro forma net debt after the October 2026 events, the covenant ratio for 30 September 2026, the executed credit documents, letters of credit issued, a credit rating and a peer set for comparison. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top Risk: support revenue erosion outrunning cloud growth while payouts continue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recurring, contracted revenue is the first strength. Cloud services and support are 80.93% of revenue and contracted revenue is USD 4.6 billion, with 57% falling within a year, so a decline in new sales does not reach cash flow quickly; this supports debt service over the next twelve months, but it does not protect the base after that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and the maturity schedule are the second strength. Cash of USD 983.29 million and an undrawn USD 750 million revolver give USD 1,733.29 million before letters of credit, no note matures before February 2028, and the October 2026 refinancing pushed the secured maturities to 2031 and 2033; pro forma net debt after the 1 and 2 October 2026 events is not established, so the benefit is stated on principal only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost discipline and light capital intensity are the third strength. Combined research and development and sales and marketing spending fell 1.75% and capital expenditure is 3.80% of revenue, so USD 807.52 million of free cash flow came from a business that needs little reinvestment; the limit is that most savings are already banked.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Proven access to secured funding is the fourth strength: the company issued 6.70% and 7.15% secured notes within a day of the quarter-end and extended its revolver to October 2031, which reduces refinancing risk before 2028 even though its coupons are higher than those on the unsecured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings base is the first weakness. Fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 1.51% was currency, constant-currency revenue fell USD 57.96 million, the latest quarter fell 4.00%, and the outlook lowers the adjusted EBITDA margin to 32% to 33%; implied adjusted EBITDA of about USD 1,677.00 million is 11.88% below fiscal 2026, so leverage rises unless debt falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Payouts are the second weakness: dividends, repurchases and treasury purchases took 91.35% of free cash flow, leaving USD 69.85 million, so debt reduction came from divestitures and cash; at the outlook midpoint of free cash flow, about USD 368.63 million remains after the dividend and amortisation, below the USD 469.31 million spent on repurchases in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2026-06-30_otex-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 236–237; 10-Q_2026-09-30_otex-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 53–54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing cost and floating-rate exposure are the third weakness: rolling USD 3,000.00 million of unsecured notes from their current coupons to 6.70% would add about USD 80.88 million a year as an illustration, and the term loan, 27.64% of principal after the October 2026 events, costs USD 15.3 million more for every rise of 100 basis points; both slow the fall in interest cost that helped cash flow in fiscal 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Unsettled financial policy and information gaps are the fourth weakness: a new chief executive, a strategic review reporting on 10 February 2027, no stated leverage target, no executed credit documents and no unaudited covenant ratio for 30 September 2026 mean creditors cannot yet price how cash will be shared with shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q1-27pressreleaseexhibit991.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
